summary: Verified BUG FIX for SSE column fill order in ARCHAUDIT. Executed 8 total audit runs against the live preview URL (3 initial + 5 confirmatory with MutationObserver). In every run the DOM appearance order was architect-loaded -> chaos-loaded -> hardened-loaded. Also verified regression items: all three columns reach loaded state with non-empty diagrams/verdicts, export-report-button is enabled, and column-*-copy buttons are present. Some runs show the amber STAGE_FAILED_SHOWING_CACHED_FALLBACK banner when NVIDIA exceeds the 25s timeout (intended behavior). No console errors observed during runs.
critical_code_review_comments: App.tsx is ~622 lines — approaching the 700-line threshold. Consider splitting column rendering / SSE stream handling into separate modules before it grows further.
SSE reader loop in executeAudit() silently swallows JSON.parse errors on malformed frames; consider surfacing a debug warning.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Column fill order was verified using a MutationObserver injected via page.evaluate that records the first appearance of each [data-testid=column-{architect|chaos|hardened}-loaded] element. This is more accurate than polling every 200ms because state updates for architect_done and attack_done can commit within a single React batch when SSE chunks arrive close together. The initial 200ms-polling test showed a false FAIL in 1/3 runs due to poll-cycle jitter; the MutationObserver approach reported 5/5 PASS with architect always ~100-300ms before chaos and hardened 7-25s later. Backend curl also confirms server-side event order is architect_done -> attack_done -> final_done. Total time per full audit: ~7-50s depending on NVIDIA response time and whether cached_fallback triggers.
rca of the issue: N/A — the bug reported in prior iterations (chaos loading before architect) is resolved. Root cause was: prior frontend rendered whichever LLM task resolved first. Fix: backend now awaits arch_task before emitting architect_done, then awaits attack_task before emitting attack_done, ensuring a fixed SSE emission order that the frontend consumes sequentially in executeAudit().
